title: A Few Design Patterns Worth Knowing
oneLiner: Not the full Gang-of-Four catalog (the 1994 book by four authors that named 23 classic patterns) -- just four patterns that show up constantly in real code, including this app's own.
keyTakeaway: A design pattern isn't a library or a language feature -- it's a NAME for a recurring shape of solution, useful specifically because naming it lets you say "this needs a Strategy" instead of re-explaining the whole idea from scratch every time.
explanation:
Design patterns aren't code you import or a language feature you turn on -- they're names for shapes of solution that keep showing up once you've written enough software, useful mainly because having a shared name for one lets a team talk about the design in one word instead of re-deriving it from scratch in every code review. The full Gang-of-Four catalog runs to over twenty patterns; four of them show up often enough to be worth knowing by name immediately, and three of the four already have a real example living somewhere in this app.

Click through the four below -- each one gets a plain description, a small code sketch, and (where it exists) the place this exact pattern already shows up elsewhere in this app or in everyday code you've probably already written without naming it.

This lesson is the short introduction. The design patterns track right after it covers the SOLID principles and seventeen patterns in depth (creational, structural and behavioral), and ends with a recognition quiz; the links under the widget jump straight to each part.
